body:
N-34 SLICE 1 IS BUILT, NOT WALKED (helper-n34s1, 16 Nov 2026; branch task/N-34-slice1-album-matcher; the item stays todo, NOT marked built: slices 2 to 7 are open). No migration, no pass, no keeper change, no real request (the 10 requests of step 0 were spent by the earlier helper).
BUILT: (1) album_finder.py, the pure matcher: judge_hits (steps 0-2, one verdict per hit with its reason), wanted_albums, choose_release (steps 3-5), RefHoldings (step 5 read from song_ref). Outcomes matched/none/held are facts; unsupported/no_length/unavailable are never remembered (Verdict.remember). (2) priority AND deadline through Catalogue._fetch/_lead/_gather/_listing/album (defaults interactive + 2.5 s, every route pinned), search_tracks(wait_s=). (3) python -m encore_server.album_dryrun, the report over a COPY of the database.
CHANGES TO THE DESIGN you should know: (a) the skip rule (survives_fold_whole, imported) is applied to EVERY HIT's artist and title too, not only the song's: the library's "Habibi" and a hit "Habibi <Arabic>" fold to the same string, so only the hit-side rule stops it (own test + mutation). Also to the album artist. (b) the single flight of Catalogue is per priority: a person opening an album is never the follower of the background pass's request for it. (c) "Unknown Artist" and names that fold to nothing (VEVO, an all-noise title) are refused at step 0 as a second layer. (d) a track list shorter than the album's trackCount that lacks the hit is track_list_cut (still none), told apart in the report.
THE TOLERANCE IS UNMEASURED (stop-gap): album_finder.TOLERANCE_MS = refs.DURATION_TOLERANCE_MS (3 s). Price: misses only (too loose = a permanent wrong id). Removal trigger: the lead reads the dry run over REAL FILES and the REAL catalogue; task: start of slice 2 freezes the constant. A copy of the database holds NO file and the server has NO file-length reader (mutagen is only used for tags): without --music-root the report measures the import's LISTING length, and says so on every histogram. First run on the copy of VM 108's DB with the 10 recorded answers: 650 songs asked-about, 3 unsupported (0.5 percent), and the listing of the Creature ref is 141 s off the catalogue's 225 s, so the listing cannot be trusted and slice 2/3 need a file-length reader (file_length_ms in album_dryrun.py is the first one; move it next to keeper/tagging.py).
HOW TO RUN ON THE REAL CATALOGUE (the lead's decision; Deezer sees that machine's address): from server/encore_server with PYTHONPATH set to it: C:\dev\venv-encore-server\Scripts\python.exe -m encore_server.album_dryrun --db <copy of encore.db> --answers <folder> --live --max-requests 2000 --out <report.txt> [--music-root <folder holding Encore/>]. About 650 searches + about 2 per distinct candidate album = roughly 1,500 requests at 4 a second = 5 to 8 minutes. Every answer is saved in --answers (a second run asks nothing; replay without --live). It stops and says so when the cap is spent or the catalogue rests the server.
FOR SLICE 2: Catalogue.album asks the song list of losing candidate albums too (one request each); asking the list only for the chosen release saves them. The pass must call album() serially (a long deadline parks one of the 6 pool workers the routes share).
Proof: 119 new tests; priority tests red on the old code for the right reasons (the new arguments did not exist) then green, 15 mutations of the plumbing killed; matcher 80 mutations killed; dry run 77 mutations killed. The run on the real DB copy found a real bug before the lead did (an Arabic title crashed the print on a cp1252 console): fixed and pinned.
